summary: Game crashes when replacing a block with a wall with blockstate up:false
description: Give yourself a wall using give p brick_wall{BlockStateTag:{up:"false"}} 1 Then, place a block with no other blocks around it, and press left and right click at the same time while looking at that block and holding the wall. Then, crash.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Ensure you are in Creative mode by running the command `/gamemode creative`.
3. Give yourself a brick_wall with the specific blockstate using the command `give p brick_wall{BlockStateTag:{up:"false"}} 1`.
4. Place any block on the ground with no other blocks around it.
5. Hold the brick_wall in your hand and look at the placed block.
6. Press left click and right click simultaneously while looking at the placed block.
7. Observe that the game crashes under these conditions.
Observed Behavior: When attempting to replace a block with a brick wall that has the `up:false` blockstate, the game crashes under specific conditions. To reproduce this issue, first give yourself a brick wall with the command `/give p brick_wall{BlockStateTag:{up:"false"}} 1`. Place this brick wall in an area where no other blocks are adjacent to it. While holding the brick wall and looking at the placed block, press both left and right mouse buttons simultaneously. This sequence of actions will cause the game to crash. This bug is specific to the `up:false` state of the brick wall and occurs only when both clicks are performed at once on a standalone block.
Expected Behavior: When attempting to replace a block with a brick wall having the blockstate `up:false`, the game should not crash. Instead, the block should be successfully replaced by the brick wall without any issues or interruptions, allowing the player to continue interacting with the environment as intended.
